text:
alex: FYI support ticket #4521 — customer CI started failing after we pushed v3.1.0 of the Go SDK. They see `module declares its path` / unknown revision errors when running go build.
support-jen: Can you paste the exact go get / go build errors and a minimal repro? Also ask them for `go env` and the root `go.mod` they used.
alex: Repro steps from the customer:
```
GO111MODULE=on go get github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3@v3.1.0
# error:
verifying github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3 v3.1.0: checksum mismatch
or
go: github.com/redwood/inference-go@v3.1.0: unknown revision v3.1.0
or
module declares its path as: github.com/redwood/inference-go/v2
```
They supplied their go.mod:
```
module example.com/customer

require (
    github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3 v3.1.0
)
```
and a snippet of `go env` (trimmed):
```
GOMODCACHE=/home/runner/go/pkg/mod
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
GOVERSION=1.20
```
support-jen: Ok. Two likely classes: tag not accessible (unknown revision) or module path inside the repo doesn't match the /v3 suffix (module declares its path ...). Can you `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood/inference-go` and `go mod download -x github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3@v3.1.0` and paste outputs? Also ask them if they or CI use a private GOPROXY.
devex-tom: Also check whether the release tag was created on the canonical repo or a fork, and whether the maintainers updated the module path in go.mod to include `/v3` (required for major v2+).
alex: Ran the checks quickly:
```
$ git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood/inference-go
... refs/tags/v3.1.0
... refs/tags/v3.1.0^{}  # annotated tag present
```
`go mod download -x` shows fetch via proxy then fails with:
```
-> GET https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3/@v3.1.0.info
<- 404 not found
fetch failed: unknown revision v3.1.0
```
But when I curl the repo URL the tag page exists on GitHub. release-kate: I pushed the release but might have done the tag from a branch in a fork and then created the GitHub Release which created a tag that points to a forked ref — hmm.
support-jen: If the tag points to a commit that's only present in a fork (not pushed upstream), `git ls-remote` against upstream would not show it — but your ls-remote above did show it. Another subtle cause: module's go.mod inside repo still declares `module github.com/redwood/inference-go` (no /v3) — that will cause the `module declares its path` error when requiring with /v3.
release-kate: Double-checked: the go.mod in the v3 branch was updated to `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3` but I think I accidentally created a lightweight tag on the monorepo root that points to a subtree commit where the go.mod still had v2 path. Oops.
devex-tom: That explains the two different errors: checksum/unknown revision comes from GOPROXY not seeing the expected metadata (maybe because proxy can't reach that specific commit structure), and the "module declares its path" comes when the versioned path inside the module doesn't include /v3.
alex: Customer's CI uses `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` so proxy behavior matters. The concrete repro to fix:
1) Ensure the canonical repo has an annotated tag `refs/tags/v3.1.0` that points to the commit where go.mod declares `/v3`.
2) If you created the tag on a branch or in a fork, push that commit to upstream and re-create the tag (annotated) on upstream.
3) Wait for proxy.golang.org to fetch the new tag (can trigger with `GOSUMDB=off GOPROXY=direct go get ...` for immediate test)

support-jen: Suggested message to customer:
"We're seeing the most common causes: either the v3 tag points to a commit where the module path wasn't updated to include /v3, or the tag wasn't available to the public proxy. Can you run `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/redwood/inference-go` and confirm it lists `refs/tags/v3.1.0` and `git show refs/tags/v3.1.0` shows a commit whose go.mod has `module github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3`? If not, we need to repush the correct tag. If it does, try `GOPROXY=direct go get ...` and paste the `go mod download -x` output so we can escalate to proxy/golang if needed."

release-kate: I deleted the lightweight tag and created an annotated tag on the correct commit, pushed to origin, and re-created the GitHub release. I also pinged mirror services. I'll follow up when proxy picks it up.
sre-bot: Reminder: create a post-release checklist item to run `go list -m -json github.com/redwood/inference-go/v3@v3.1.0` in CI to validate module path and tag propagation.

alex: Customer confirmed `GOPROXY=direct` build now succeeds and `go list -m` returns v3.1.0 with correct module path. Closing ticket once mirrors settle. :thumbsup:
support-jen: Nice root-cause and mitigation. We'll add a quick checkbox in the release guide: update go.mod module path for major bumps, tag annotated on upstream commit, verify `go list -m -json` before announcing.
